Definition: to strip off, i.e. generally to make naked (for exertion or in disgrace), to drain away or bail up (a liquid)
BiblicalUsage: 1) to strip, strip off, lay bare, make bare, draw out; 1a) (Qal); 1a1) to strip off; 1a2) to strip, lay bare; 1a3) to draw (water), skim, take from the surface
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
